title: quantization-nan-debug-scratchpad-maya-2026-03-25
content:
SUMMARY:
Fast scratchpad for ongoing NaN/quality regressions observed after adding mixed FP8/INT8 weight pipelines. Mostly reproducing on long-context sampling (seq_len > 2048) on rtx-a100 clusters but occasionally on small sequences during stress tests.

TIMELINE
- 2026-03-20: New FP8 quantization code merged to branch quant/fp8-experimental (PR#289). Minimal unit tests passed.
- 2026-03-22: First customer report: occasional output collapse / NaN tokens when sampling with temperature=0.8, beam=1 (hosted).
- 2026-03-23: Reproduced locally with our sampling harness using seq_len=4096 and batch_size=4 — NaNs appear after ~120 tokens.
- 2026-03-25: Started systematic triage below.

REPRO STEPS (what I run locally)
- convert and run with same config as failing job:
  # convert float32 -> fp8 mixed weights (experimental converter)
  python tools/quantize_weights.py --model checkpoints/llama-13b/ --out q/llama-13b-fp8 --format fp8 --group-size 32 --calib-data data/calib_small.json

  # run the inference server locally (dev image)
  ./scripts/run_local_server.sh --model q/llama-13b-fp8 --device cuda:0 --batch 4 --max-seq 4096 --sampling 

  # or run sampling harness directly
  python tools/sample_harness.py --model q/llama-13b-fp8 --prompt-file prompts/customer_issue.txt --length 512 --temperature 0.8 --seed 42

OBSERVED ERRORS / SNIPPETS
- Typical log around failure:
  [2026-03-25 14:12:03] SAMPLE: token=120 loss=nan
  [2026-03-25 14:12:03] WARNING: kv_cache invalid values detected (inf/nan)
  traceback (most recent call last):
    File "runtime/decoder.cu", line 412, in update_kv_cache
    CHECK(!isnan(value));
  RuntimeError: kernel failure: NAN encountered in add_kernel at 0x7f...

- CUDA device-side prints show some large values before collapse:
  layer 18 attn_score max=1.2e19 min=-2.1e19
  layer 18 attn_softmax sum=nan

HYPOTHESES (ranked)
1) FP8 dynamic range / scaling mismatch for attention matmuls when using hybrid INT8 weights in some layers -> overflow during accumulation (kernel uses fp16 accumulation path but quant scale incorrect).
2) KV cache write path incorrectly assuming fp16 intermediate; mixing BF16/FP8 code paths leads to uninitialized memory on warp boundaries.
3) LayerNorm implementation numerical instability with quantized weights (scale small -> divide by near-zero variance) -> NaN propagates.
4) Bug in conversion tool: for group_size boundaries the clip/scale table has off-by-one producing extremely large dequantized weights for last column of some rows.
5) Sampling temperature / top-k interplay reveals rare path where logits become very large due to attention score blowup.

EXPERIMENTS TRIED (results)
- Re-run with accumulation in FP32 (force-accum-fp32=True) -> failure no longer reproduces in short runs (seq<=1024) but still shows collapse for 4096 after ~350 tokens. Suggests accumulation precision helps but not full fix.
- Force all layers to BF16 (no FP8/INT8 mixing) -> stable.
- Disable KV cache (recompute keys each step) -> no NaNs in long run (slower but suggests write-to-cache path implicated).
- Add guard clamp after softmax: if any nan or inf in attn_softmax then set to uniform -> masks NaN but hides root cause.
- Run conversion with group-size=1 -> still reproduces. group-size=64 -> reproduces faster.

Additional log excerpt (debug dump for layer 18 before collapse):
- W (dequantized) max=3.4e38 (suspicious), min=-3.4e38
- observed quant scale table entries for last group: [0.00023, 0.00012, 1.7e+38] <-- that 1.7e+38 looks like uninitialized/overflow sentinel

PRIORITY TODOs / NEXT STEPS
- [ ] Add assert/validation in converter: no scale > 1e6 and no NaN/INF entries in scale table. (high priority)
- [ ] Instrument runtime to dump scale table and quant metadata per-layer when loading quantized model (low overhead).
- [ ] Add unit test that dequantizes random groups and checks for staggering magnitudes (CI).
- [ ] Reproduce minimal test-case: single-matrix multiply with same quant scales + random inputs until overflow. Create C++ microbench to match kernel accumulator path.
- [ ] Validate KV-cache write routine (write atomicity / alignment) for mixed-width stores across warp lanes.
- [ ] If converter is at fault, roll back FP8 flag for hosted experiments and patch conversion.

Notes / random observations:
- Customer config used batch=8 on dedicated GPU (A100-80GB), seq=8192, using dedicated fp8 pipeline. They see collapse after ~200 tokens.
- Memory pattern: free memory drops by ~1GB right before NaN event (maybe extra allocation request triggers some path?).
- I saw one stack where a memset was using size computed from dtype size (assuming 4 bytes for fp32) but used on fp8 buffer -> potential memory corruption.

Link to minimal reproducer work-in-progress: github.com/redwood-inference/rt/quant-repro (WIP, branch maya/nan-debug)

Slack notes: pinged #eng-serving-runtime and #applied-ml with logs; Arjun saw similar behavior on his machine and will try reproducer on V100.

If stuck: next escalate to runtime team and consider toggling fallback to BF16 by default for hosted API until we have stronger CI and converter checks.

-- Maya
